To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
nrde-1; nrde-3 double mutants are broadly defective in RNAi, and that nrde- 3 is required to silence repetitive transgenes and to trigger transitive RNAi.
NRDE- 3 is a limiting RNAi resource required for eri- dependent RNAi and that NRDE- dependent RNAi contributes to transitive silencing.

the nuclear RNA interference defective-3 (nrde-3) mutant phenotype extends to include a broader set of RNAi phenomena, and that the nuclear Argonaute NRDe-3 contributes to endogenous siRNA-dependent silencing and transitive RNAi.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the discovery of new components of RNA interference and the characterization of their function in RNAi.
how RNA silencing pathways are regulated in C. elegans.
the mechanisms, roles and functions of nuclear Argonaute-mediated RNA silencing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
nrde-1 and nrde-3 are required for transitive silencing, but only in the presence of ERI-1 and PGL-1.
the nrde-3 mutant is broadly RNAi deficient.
nrde- 3 mutants are broadly deficient for RNAi and that nrde-1 and nrde-3 are limiting RNAi resource genes that act in separate pathways to enhance RNA silencing in C. elegans.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
nrde-2 and nrde-3 are required for the full range of RNAi phenomena, including endogenous siRNA-mediated silencing, transitive RNAi amplification, and ERI-dependent silencing.

NRDE-2 and NRDE-3 are both required for endogenous RNA silencer function, and NRDE-2 is required for the amplification of RNA silencer signals, while NRDE-3 functions to limit primary transcript production.
NRDE-1, NRDE-3, and PGL-1 are all limiting resources for effective RNAi and that these three proteins act in separate, nonoverlapping pathways.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nrde mutants are broadly RNA interference deficient, which suggests that NRDE-1, -2, and -3 act in multiple endogenous RNA silencers to regulate gene expression.
nrde-1 and nrde-3 define distinct RNAi pathways that act in cis to silence transcripts and in trans to silence transgenes, respectively.
the nuclear RNAi pathway is a broadly important contributor to RNAi in Caenohabditis elegans.
